component: Local policy and federation floor stores and their shared transaction core
constraints: One row per protected local file; current format/scope validation, monotonic time/revision, exact digest and same-revision equivocation rejection. Policy v1 and federation v1 remain disjoint.
Atomic cooperating-process read/check/write; fixed errors, no retries, exclusive initialization and no silent reset. Correct local locks/flushes and authenticated inputs are caller preconditions.
Offline Python 3.9+ API with optional SQLite >=3.31; no hard completion-time, target hardware or latency budget established.
alternatives: Native SQLite with Python sqlite3, Rust rusqlite explicit Result-returning close, or C#/F# Microsoft.Data.Sqlite transactions.
Erlang/Elixir Mnesia transactions and managed processes for a different local/distributed storage deployment.
Atomic file replacement plus an explicit interprocess lock and journal/recovery protocol.
LMDB is a credible embedded transaction candidate; earlier source retrieval failed, so no unsupported API or performance comparison is credited.
rationale: KEEP SQLite and its current binding for both profiles: database transactions provide the required local read/check/write serialization; direct bounded validator calls avoid a second parsing/serialization boundary. Another binding does not itself establish whole-store rollback detection or authenticated storage.

Mnesia is credible when managed/distributed state is required; that is not this single-row local profile. Atomic replacement still requires a separate cooperating-writer transaction protocol. No measured language or storage speed ranking is asserted.

FIX the shared cleanup boundary: injected SQLite/OS errors from close previously escaped as raw backend exceptions. Translate them to fixed store_unavailable, suppress backend context and return no success metadata.

Real-file tests prove that cleanup errors after commit can coexist with persisted time or deny-all federation updates; errors must not be interpreted as rollback. Existing wire formats and disk schemas remain unchanged.
limits: Injection performs real close then raises; it is not an observed operating-system fault, power-loss test or demonstration that standard close normally fails.
A failing close does not guarantee resource release. Whole-file restoration can restore old floors; no coordinated two-file transaction, authentication or encryption is added.
Alternative candidates were source-compared, not executed or benchmarked. No hard-real-time, physical, MLS/CNSA or availability qualification.
